lines.text: Come here, little one... shall I teach you chess?
Yes please, Grandpa!
Sixty-four squares on a board, dark and light,
With a light corner square at the bottom right,
Two little armies, all lined up in rows,
Each piece is different, and here's how it goes!
Pawn and Knight and Bishop,
Rook and Queen and King!
Each has its own special way to move,
And together they make the game sing!
The Pawn is like dawn, it's where morning begins,
It only moves forward, and never gives in,
One step at a time, on its first go, take two!
And it captures on slants, just one square, as pawns do.
The Knight is a night with a K at the start,
A horse that can leap, and that's the trickiest part!
Two squares, then a turn, in the shape of an L,
The only one jumping, and oh, it jumps well!
The Bishop's tall hat is the shape of a drop,
It zooms on the slant till a piece makes it stop,
Corner to corner, like a slide in the park,
It stays on its colour, the light or the dark!
Look at the Rook, it's a tower of stone,
It starts in the corner, the corner's its home,
It runs in straight lines like a train on a track,
Up, down, and sideways, and all the way back!
Pawn and Knight and Bishop,
Rook and Queen and King!
Each has its own special way to move,
And together they make the game sing!
The Queen is the strongest, so graceful and free,
Straight lines or slanting, as far as can be,
She's a Rook and a Bishop, both rolled into one,
So keep her safe early, the game's just begun!
The King's very slow, just one square any way,
Like Grandpa in slippers at the end of the day,
But he matters the most: trapped in check? That's checkmate!
So guard yours, and catch theirs, before it's too late!
Rooks in the corners, then Knights by their side,
Bishops come next with their hats held with pride,
The Queen on her colour, the King takes the last,
And the Pawns fill the front row, standing brave, standing fast!
Just six kinds of pieces on sixty-four squares,
Yet more games to play than the stars way up there,
Each game is a story that's new, never told,
So set up the board, let the next one unfold!
Now here is a secret, the best one of all:
The Pawn may be little, the Pawn may be small,
But step after step, if it reaches the end,
It can grow to a Queen, so keep marching, my friend.
Pawn and Knight and Bishop,
Rook and Queen and King!
Even the smallest can wear a crown,
So come, let the whole board sing!
So come, let the whole board sing!
Your move, Grandpa!
